info.title: AGI Workforce API
info.description:
OpenAI-compatible inference gateway, the billing and device-authorization endpoints the first-party apps use, and the workspace administration API.

The complete API base URL is `https://agiworkforce.com/api`. The API host also exposes the OpenAI-compatible aliases `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, and `/v1/credits/balance` at `https://api.agiworkforce.com`, plus `/health`. Other operations use the complete API base URL above.

Three credential types authenticate here and they are NOT interchangeable. An AGI API key (`sk_live_…`/`sk_test_…`, issued under Settings > API Keys) works only on the operations that declare `ApiKeyAuth`. A workspace API key (`agiadm_…`, issued in the workspace console under Audit > Workspace API keys) works only on the workspace administration operations that declare `WorkspaceApiKeyAuth`. Every other operation needs a session bearer token. Each operation states which one it takes. Rate limits are published in `docs/standards/api-rate-limits.md`.

BearerAuth.description: Session bearer token, a Clerk session JWT or a first-party device token. Browser requests may present the session cookie instead. AGI API keys are rejected wherever this is the only accepted scheme.

ApiKeyAuth.description: AGI API key (`sk_live_…` / `sk_test_…`) issued in the developer console at /developers. Scopes are chosen at issue time; an operation lists the one it needs in `x-agi-api-key-scope` and answers 403 `insufficient_scope` without it.

WorkspaceApiKeyAuth.description: Workspace API key (`agiadm_…`) issued in the workspace console under Audit > Workspace API keys. It acts for the workspace rather than for a person, keeps working after the member who issued it leaves, and needs an active Team or Enterprise plan. The issuer picks its scopes, only from permissions they hold, and an optional expiry; neither can change after issue, and the key can be revoked at any time. An operation names the scope it needs in `x-agi-workspace-scope` and answers 403 without it, listing the scopes the key carries. A revoked, expired or unknown key answers 401, and a call from outside the workspace's IP allow list answers 403 `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`. Writes made with a key need no CSRF token.

billingInterval.description: Billing cycle interval. Individual plans (basic, pro, max, max_15x) are sold monthly only and refuse yearly with a 400; team is sold monthly or yearly.

seats.description: Licensed seat count. Required for per-seat plans (team) and rejected for per-account plans. Charged as the Stripe line-item quantity.

plan.description: The plan to move the active subscription to. For team, the same plan with a larger seats value adds seats.

billingInterval.description: Must match the current subscription's cadence when the target plan sells that cadence; a mismatch answers 400.

seats.description: Licensed seat count for team. Seats can only increase; added seats keep the renewal date and are charged for the rest of the current period.

promotionCode.description: Optional customer-facing promotion code, checked with Stripe before it is quoted.

UpgradePreview.description: The exact charge an upgrade would make. A tier upgrade starts a new billing period today: the new plan's price minus a credit for the unused time on the current plan. A seat increase keeps the renewal date and charges only for the rest of the period.

amountDueNowCents.description: What is charged today, after tax and any balance.

charge.description: Itemized receipt: lineItems, subtotalCents, discountCents, taxCents, totalCents, appliedBalanceCents, totalDueTodayCents, creditToBalanceCents and renewsAt.

recurringAmountCents.description: What renews each period after the upgrade, before tax.

promotion.description: The applied promotion code and its discount, when one was sent.

previewToken.description: Signed quote to send to POST /upgrade. It binds the plan, cadence, seats, promotion and proration time.

UpgradeCheckoutRequired.description: The account has no paid subscription to credit, so the plan must be bought through POST /checkout. `checkout` quotes that purchase.

previewToken.description: The previewToken from POST /upgrade/preview for the same plan, cadence, seats and promotion.

activation.description: Stripe has charged; the plan is written when its subscription event arrives, usually within seconds.

UpgradePaymentActionRequired.description: The bank asked for authentication. Finish the payment at paymentUrl, or confirm clientSecret with Stripe.js, before the plan activates.

device_fingerprint.description: Optional device fingerprint used to prevent unauthorized polling

link_code.description: The code the user should approve

device_id.description: Device identifier associated with this code

verify_url.description: URL where user can verify the device

ApiError.description: OpenAI-shaped error envelope returned by the inference endpoints.

resets_at.description: On a plan-limit refusal, when the refusing window resets: the oldest usage leaving a rolling 5-hour or weekly window, the end of the billing period, or the start of the next month for a monthly allowance.

alternative_model.description: On a plan-limit refusal, a model the caller's plan can use now: a standard model when a flagship limit refused, or a free-pool model when a usage window or the billing period refused. Absent when none is eligible.

RateLimitError.description: Body of a 429. `retry_after_seconds` mirrors the `Retry-After` header; see docs/standards/api-rate-limits.md for the per-endpoint ceilings.

Model.description: OpenAI-compatible model record, extended with the catalog fields a router needs.

tier.description: Lowest plan that may select this model.

image_detail.description: The image `detail` values this model accepts, from the model registry. Present only on models the registry records; a model without it accepts `auto`, `low` and `high`.

capabilities.description: What the model accepts and produces, from the model registry. `null` means the registry has no verified answer.

deprecation_date.description: The day this model stops being served, published while it is still listed so callers can move before then. `null` when no retirement is scheduled.

routing_profiles.description: The values `routing_profile` accepts on chat completions, with the label and description a picker can show.

model.description: A model id from GET /llm/v1/models, or an auto mode from `x_agi_workforce.allowed_auto_modes`.

content.description: A string, or the OpenAI content-part array (`text`, `image_url`, `file`). An `image_url` part may set `detail` to `auto`, `low` or `high`, or to `original` on a model the registry lists for original-resolution image inspection (listed in `image_detail` by `GET /llm/v1/models`). A detail value the model does not accept answers 400 `image_detail_unsupported`.

stream.description: Streams the answer as server-sent `chat.completion.chunk` events. Besides the OpenAI fields, a chunk's `choices[].delta` may carry these extensions: `x_tool_status` ({`type`, `name`, `status` of `running`, `completed` or `failed`, and on `running` an optional `status_phrase` and the parsed `args`}) for each tool call; `x_agent_event`, a versioned envelope ({`schemaVersion`, `sessionId`, `turnId`, `sequence`, `emittedAtMs`, `event`}) for agent steps, approvals and tool progress; `x_search_results` with the sources a web search returned; `x_tool_result` ({`tool_call_id`, `name`, `content`, `is_error`}) once a tool has run, with `content` the text the model receives; and `x_generated_files` ({`files`}) when the turn created a file. When a connector tool needs the user to connect or reconnect an account, its `x_tool_result` has `is_error` true and `content` a JSON object: {`agi_connector_authorization_required`: true, `connectorId`, `connectorName`, `toolName`, `reason` (`not_connected`, `authorization_expired`, `insufficient_scope` or `authorization_unavailable`), `connectUrl`, `scopes`, `message`}. `connectUrl` is a path on the server's origin, such as `/api/connectors/oauth/start?connectorId=<connectorId>`: resolve it against the server URL and open it in a browser where the user is signed in, then send the request again to continue. It is null when this deployment cannot connect that connector. A client that does not know an extension can ignore it.

top_p.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

n.description: Only 1 is supported, because each request returns one completion. A larger value answers 400 `unsupported_parameter`.

seed.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

stop.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

presence_penalty.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

frequency_penalty.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

logit_bias.description: Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

user.description: An opaque identifier for your end user, passed to providers that accept one for abuse monitoring. Do not send names or email addresses. Forwarded to the provider when the serving model accepts it; a model that does not answers 400 `unsupported_parameter` naming it. `/llm/v1/models` lists each model's accepted parameters as `request_parameters`.

response_format.description: `text`, `json_object` and `json_schema` are honoured. `json_object` and `json_schema` need `stream: false`, because the reply is validated before it is returned. With `json_schema` the reply is checked against the schema, and a reply that does not satisfy it answers 502 `json_schema_not_satisfied` rather than returning unvalidated output. It works with image input on any model the registry marks for both vision and structured output; a model without structured output answers 400 `model_no_structured_output`. When the registry marks the serving model for structured output and its provider offers a native JSON mode, the request also asks the provider for that mode.

schema.description: A JSON Schema whose root has type `object`. Supported keywords: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, const, anyOf, $defs and local $ref, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, minItems, maxItems, pattern, format, description, title and default. Any other keyword is refused with 400.

memory_enabled.description: Whether this request may read the memories saved in your account. A request made with an API key reads none unless this is `true`, and it never saves new memories or searches past chats. Has no effect while Memory is off in your account settings.

web_search.description: Runs a hosted web search for this turn and cites what it found. When omitted, search turns on if the prompt asks to search or the task is research; `false` keeps it off. Each search is charged as Agentic search.

research.description: Runs Deep Research: the model plans, searches and reads many sources before it writes a cited report. A model that cannot run research answers the request normally instead. Searches are billed as Agentic search.

research_sources.description: What a Deep Research run may read when `research` is true. `allow_domains` and `deny_domains` also apply to ordinary `web_search`: they are passed to the search backend as its domain filter and every result is checked against them before the model sees it, so a page outside the allowed sites or on a denied one is never returned. `files` applies only to Deep Research.

files.description: Also search the documents indexed in your account.

allow_domains.description: Only read and cite pages on these sites, for example `nature.com`.

deny_domains.description: Never read or cite pages on these sites.

connectors.description: Connected apps to search for the run's planned questions, by connector id. An app is read through the MCP `search` and `fetch` tools deep research servers expose; one that offers no `search` tool, or is not connected to your account, is named in the report as not searched. Applies only to Deep Research.

research_resume.description: Continues a Deep Research run that stopped for its plan to be approved, or that failed or was stopped. Applies only when `research` is true.

sources.description: Sources the run had already gathered, so they are not fetched again.

retrieved_at.description: When the run first retrieved this source, so the resumed run keeps that date instead of the time it resumed.

approved_steps.description: The plan to run, as you approved or edited it. The run follows these steps instead of the proposed ones.

guidance.description: Guidance for the rest of the run, sent when it resumes. It is added to the plan as a step and the searches still to run are re-planned to follow it.

deliverable.description: What the finished report should be.

minSources.description: Distinct sources the run must have before it finishes; 0 sets no floor.

stopWhenNoNewSources.description: Stop gathering once a round finds no new source.

saveToLibrary.description: Also keep the finished report in your Library.

personalization.description: `false` answers without your account's personalization: no custom instructions, profile or response style, and no memory is read or saved for this request. Omitted or `true` keeps the default.

web_fetch.description: Lets the model open a web page or document named in the conversation and read it. Web pages, plain text, Markdown, JSON, PDFs and Word, Excel or PowerPoint files are read as text; images, audio and video are refused. When omitted on a streamed request, it turns on if the prompt asks to open a link.

code_execution.description: Offers the model code execution for this turn. When omitted on a streamed request, it turns on if the prompt asks to run code or analyse data. The sandbox file tools (`read_file`, `write_file`, `edit_file`) run only where this deployment has sandbox execution enabled; elsewhere the tool answers that they are unavailable.

office_creation.description: Offers the model a tool that creates a downloadable `docx`, `pptx`, `xlsx`, `pdf` or `csv` file. A streamed response announces each file in an `x_generated_files` delta. When omitted on a streamed request, it turns on if the prompt asks to create one of those files.

connector_tools_enabled.description: A request made with an API key can use the connectors connected to the account. The model sees their tools by name and loads a tool's schema on demand with `load_connector_tools`, by exact name or by a keyword query that returns the best matches with their descriptions. A connector call that needs approval pauses the run, and `POST /llm/v1/chat/completions/approve` resumes it. `false` offers no connector tools for this turn.

disabled_connector_ids.description: Connector ids whose tools are not offered for this turn.

skill_name.description: Runs this turn with one of the skills your account can use, named as it appears in Settings > Skills (for example `document-creation`). The model loads the skill before it answers. Answers 422 with `skill_not_found` when the skill is not installed for your account, `skill_model_unsupported` when the chosen model cannot use tools, and `skill_requirements_unmet` when the skill needs a tool or connector that is off for this turn.

routing_profile.description: How Auto chooses a model when `model` is `auto`. `speed` routes to the quickest models your plan includes, `quality` to the most capable one your plan allows (a plan's ceiling still applies, so Pro is served its best balanced model), and `cost` to the lowest-cost model that can handle the task. `auto`, or leaving it out, lets Auto decide per message. Ignored when `model` names a specific model. Workspace model policy, data residency and the training opt-out still limit every choice.

ChatCompletionResponse.description: OpenAI-compatible completion. When `stream` is true the response is `text/event-stream` of `chat.completion.chunk` events terminated by `data: [DONE]` instead.

x_agi_workforce.description: Gateway metadata: the provider that served the turn and the routing decision behind it.

input.description: One string, or a batch of at most 100, each at most 32000 characters.

encoding_format.description: `base64` is rejected, not ignored, a caller expecting base64 must not receive floats.

selection.description: Model key or Auto alias to preview. Defaults to the Auto policy's default alias.

taskType.description: A routing task type from the Auto policy.

conversationId.description: When given, the conversation's served route affinity informs the preview.

capabilitiesInUse.description: Intrinsic capability names from the model registry the conversation relies on. A route observed failing one is excluded.

selected.description: The Auto route decision for the request.

liveRequestExecuted.description: Always false: a preview never reaches a provider.

CreditBalance.description: Percentage-only managed-usage status. Ledger units and allocations never cross this boundary.

ManagedUsageSummary.description: Percentage-only managed-usage summary across every rolling window. Ledger units and allocations never cross this boundary.

voice.description: Voice name. An unknown name falls back to the default voice.

conversationId.description: Conversation the session belongs to. Used only to fingerprint the reservation.

LiveVoiceSessionSettlement.description: Reservation handle for the session. Return it verbatim when closing the session; without it the reservation is only released when its lease expires.

ceilingSeconds.description: Seconds the reservation covers. A close report is billed at this ceiling at most.

seconds.description: Seconds the session ran. Billed seconds are this rounded up, capped at the reserved ceiling.

backend.description: What the delegated backend model spent during the session. Omit it when the session delegated nothing; the session itself still settles.

credits.description: Credits charged, to two decimal places

key.description: Workload, model id or project id

byWorkload.description: Usage by product area, including research

byProject.description: Usage by project; turns outside a project are not included

WorkspaceApiError.description: Error envelope of the workspace administration and account settings endpoints. `error.code` is stable and `error.message` is safe to show. A browser session whose write fails the CSRF check gets `error` as a string and `code` beside it.

details.description: The fields a 400 rejected, when the request failed validation.

code.description: `CSRF_VALIDATION_FAILED` when a browser session sent no valid `x-csrf-token`.

provisioningSource.description: How the membership was created, for example `manual`, `invitation` or `scim`. A SCIM-provisioned member is managed by the directory.

hasMore.description: Whether another page follows this one.

lastId.description: Pass as `afterId` to read the next page.

warnings.description: Credentials that could not be revoked. The member is out of the workspace either way.

invitedByUserId.description: The member who sent it, or `service_principal:<id>` when a workspace API key did.

lastId.description: Pass as `afterId` to read the next page.

inviteToken.description: Returned once. It opens the invitation only for the invited address; deliver it yourself when `delivery.emailSent` is false.

results.description: One row per member with settled usage that day, highest credits first. Empty on a day without usage.

nextPage.description: Pass as `page`, with the same `from` and `to`, to read the next day buckets.

result.description: The run's output, with `text` for the answer and `usage` for what it cost

output.description: The run's answer, the same text as `result.text`. Null while the run is going, when it failed or was cancelled, and when it only recorded a skip.

pendingApproval.description: Present while the run waits for the owner's approval: when it was requested, when it expires, and each step it is waiting on

replay.description: True when this Idempotency-Key had already started the run

run_id.description: The `X-AGI-Agent-Run-Id` header of the stream that paused

tool_approvals.description: One decision per paused call. Every pending call of the run must be answered.

guidance.description: Optional text the agent reads before it continues, for example what to do instead of a denied call. Guidance that contains a secret is refused with 400.

detached.description: `true` when the caller will not read the stream. The run then finishes even if the connection closes; follow it at the `X-AGI-Agent-Run-URL` response header. Omitted or `false` stops the run when the connection closes.

guidance.description: Optional text the agent reads before it continues.

input_responses.description: The answers the connector asked for, passed to it verbatim. At most 16,000 characters once serialized.

detached.description: `true` when the caller will not read the stream. The run then finishes even if the connection closes; follow it at the `X-AGI-Agent-Run-URL` response header. Omitted or `false` stops the run when the connection closes.

device_id.description: Must be the device the step was issued to

level.description: `allow` runs the tool without asking, `ask` asks every time, `deny` never runs it. A saved `allow` still asks when the call would send private data out after reading untrusted content.

XQuotaWarning.description: Sent when this request is projected to take the account to 80% or more of a usage window. Semicolon-separated fields: level (warning from 80%, critical from 95%), scope (billing_period, rolling_five_hour or rolling_weekly, whichever is fullest), used_percent after this request, and threshold_percent. Absent below 80% and on plans without usage limits.

get.description: Models the caller may select, in OpenAI `/v1/models` shape. Callers with no `Authorization` header get the free catalog; a credential that fails to verify is rejected rather than downgraded to it, so a revoked key never looks like a lost entitlement.

200.description: Model list for the caller's tier

403.description: API key lacks the `models:read` scope

post.description:
OpenAI-compatible chat completions, streaming or buffered.

Takes an AGI API key or a session bearer token. A key is always pinned to the `api` client surface regardless of any `x-agi-surface` header, and that surface is gated on the `managed_api` plan capability, so a key on a plan without it answers 403 `managed_api_plan_required`.

When a tool call needs the user's approval, a streamed turn emits a chunk whose `choices[0].delta.x_agent_event.event` has `type: "approval-requested"` with `approvalId`, `toolCallId`, `name`, `category`, `summary`, `input` and, on a high-risk call, `riskLevel: "high"`, then ends. The `X-AGI-Agent-Run-Id` response header names the paused run. Answer it with `POST /llm/v1/chat/completions/approve` within 24 hours.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Required with a session bearer token. Optional with an AGI API key: when it is absent the gateway assigns the request its own key, so a retry is billed as a new request. Reuse a key only to retry the same body. `GET /usage/turns/{requestId}` looks up the credits a request settled at by the key it was sent with.

200.description: Completion, or an SSE stream when `stream` is true

400.description: Invalid request body

403.description: API key lacks the `inference:write` scope, or the calling plan lacks the capability for the resolved client surface

404.description: The addressed resource does not exist for this caller

409.description: The resource is in a state this operation cannot be applied to

413.description: Uploaded payload is larger than this endpoint accepts

499.description: Client closed the connection before the response finished streaming

502.description: Upstream provider returned a response this gateway could not use

503.description: No provider was available to serve the request

504.description: Upstream provider did not answer inside the gateway timeout

post.description: OpenAI-compatible embeddings. Takes a session bearer token only: the route declares no API-key scope, so a key is refused at the auth gate. `Idempotency-Key` is required so a retry settles the reservation once.

200.description: Embedding vectors, indexed to the input batch

400.description: Invalid embeddings request

post.description: OpenAI-compatible transcription. The upload is capped at 25 MB and its first bytes are sniffed, so a declared audio MIME type on non-audio content is rejected.

model.description: A live OpenAI speech-to-text model id. Anything else falls back to the default transcription model.

400.description: Missing file or unparseable form data

403.description: API key lacks the `inference:write` scope

415.description: Unsupported audio type, or content that is not audio

post.description: Resolves the route Auto would take for a selection and task type under the caller's plan, workspace policy, zero-data-retention posture and observed route health, without executing a request. The same auth gate and rate limits as `POST /chat/completions` apply.

200.description: The selected route, the candidates considered and the routes excluded

400.description: Invalid request body or unknown routing task type

403.description: Subscription inactive, workspace policy refused the caller, or the API key lacks the `inference:write` scope

get.description: Percentage-only managed-usage status for the calling account, plus when it resets.

403.description: No subscription record, or the API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

post.description: Exchanges a WebRTC offer for an answer and opens a live voice session against the `voice_live` routing slot, with the delegated backend on the `voice_live_backend` slot. The session is reserved for a fixed block of minutes before any provider spend, and that reservation is released if the provider never answers. Close the session to settle it.

201.description: The WebRTC answer, the session id and the reservation handle to settle with

400.description: No WebRTC offer, or an offer the schema rejects

402.description: Managed usage is exhausted for the plan window

403.description: Workspace policy, spend limit or model policy refused the caller, the account is not entitled to managed compute, or the API key lacks the `inference:write` scope

429.description: Rate limited, or the voice-minute allowance for the plan is spent

502.description: The live voice service answered without a session

503.description: Live voice is not configured on the server, or managed usage billing is unavailable

post.summary: Close and settle a live voice session
post.description: Reports how long the session ran and settles its reservation. Billed seconds are the reported seconds rounded up, capped at the ceiling the reservation covers, so a lost or exaggerated report never bills above the reserved block. Reported backend spend is recorded against cost of goods separately from the per-minute session rate.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session id returned when the session was opened

400.description: No usage report, or a report the schema rejects

403.description: The credential resolves to a different account than the reservation, or the API key lacks the `inference:write` scope

get.description: Percentage-only managed-usage summary for the calling account across every rolling window, plus the subscription state those windows are measured against. Ledger units and allocations never cross this boundary.

403.description: API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

get.description: What the calling account's settled managed usage went on across a window, in credits: request and credit totals, a series by UTC day, week or month, and breakdowns by workload, by model and by project, with how fresh the figures are. Without a window it covers the last 30 days by day, the last 12 weeks by week, or the last 12 months by month.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the window, ISO 8601

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the window, ISO 8601

parameters.name: granularity
parameters.description: How to group the series: day (the default), week or month, in UTC

403.description: API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

post.summary: Estimate the credits a chat completion will cost
post.description: Takes the body you would send to chat completions and returns an estimated credit range, counted on the model's list price with no provider call and no charge. The minimum is the input alone and the maximum adds max_tokens of output, or the model's default output ceiling. Input tokens are estimated from the text of the messages and tools you send, so server-added instructions and images are not counted. It follows Anthropic's token counting endpoint (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting): same body as the request it estimates, an estimate rather than a bill, free and rate limited separately from completions.

model.description: The model id the completion would use

400.description: The body is not a chat completions body, or the model is unknown or has no published per-token price

403.description: API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

get.description: Voice minutes, video seconds and computer-use requests used this calendar month against the calling account's plan allowance, the images generated this month with their credits, the instant the monthly allowances reset, and how many managed responses are running now against the plan's concurrent limit. A null hard limit means the plan sets no monthly cap.

403.description: API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

get.summary: Get the settled cost of a request
get.description: The credits a managed request settled at, looked up by the Idempotency-Key it was sent with. status is pending while the request is still running or settling, with credits null; poll until it is settled. A request that failed or was released settles at 0 credits.

parameters.name: requestId
parameters.description: The Idempotency-Key the request was sent with

400.description: The request ID is not a valid Idempotency-Key

403.description: API key lacks the `usage:read` scope

404.description: No managed request with that ID exists on this account

post.description: Initiate a Stripe checkout session for subscription

400.description: Invalid request parameters

403.description: Paid upgrades are gated: the account has no waitlist access or invite code yet, or may not start checkout for this subscription

post.summary: Quote an upgrade or a seat increase
post.description: Prices a change to the caller's active Stripe subscription without charging: a tier upgrade, or more seats on Team. Returns an itemized charge and a previewToken for POST /upgrade. An account with no paid subscription to credit answers 409 checkout_required and buys through POST /checkout.

400.description: Invalid request, a cadence the upgrade must keep, fewer seats, or a promotion code that does not apply

409.description: No paid subscription to credit (checkout_required, with a checkout quote), or a cancellation is pending

503.description: Billing could not be verified; nothing was changed

post.summary: Apply a quoted upgrade or seat increase
post.description: Charges the saved payment method for the change quoted by POST /upgrade/preview and updates the subscription. The previewToken must match the plan, cadence, seats and promotion, and the charge is the one the quote stated.

200.description: Charged; the plan activates when the subscription event arrives

400.description: Invalid request, an expired or mismatched previewToken, or a change the plan does not allow

402.description: The bank asked for authentication before the charge completes

409.description: No paid subscription to credit (checkout_required) or a cancellation is pending

503.description: Billing could not be verified; nothing was charged

post.description: Create a device authorization code for linking a new device

400.description: Invalid device parameters

post.description: Check if a device has been authorized by the user

403.description: Device fingerprint mismatch

404.description: The addressed resource does not exist for this caller

410.description: The device authorization code has expired and cannot be polled again

post.summary: Approve or deny a device authorization code
post.description: Approve (or deny) a device-link code so the device can retrieve a one-time session token.

403.description: Credential verified but is not permitted to perform this operation

patch.description: Sets the member's role to `admin`, `member` or `viewer` and records `member_role_changed` in the audit trail. Ownership moves only through the transfer flow, so `owner` answers 409, and the owner's own role cannot be changed here. Only a caller who holds every permission of the admin role can grant it. A workspace API key assigns only `member` and `viewer`, and cannot change an owner, an admin, or a member whose roles grant admin permissions; make those changes in the workspace console. A browser session sends `x-csrf-token`.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The member's user id, as `userId` in the member list

200.description: The member with the new role

400.description: The body is not a known role

401.description: No credential, or a workspace API key that is invalid, expired or revoked

403.description: The workspace is not on a Team or Enterprise plan, the request came from outside the workspace's IP allow list, the caller lacks the permission or the `admin.members.manage` scope, the caller lacks a permission of the admin role it tried to grant, only an owner may change an owner, or a workspace API key tried to assign `admin` or to change an owner, an admin, or a member whose roles grant admin permissions. A browser session without a valid `x-csrf-token` also gets 403, as does a write with no credential at all

A caller cannot remove themselves (they leave the workspace instead), and the last owner cannot be removed. A workspace API key removes only members and viewers whose roles grant no admin permissions. A browser session sends `x-csrf-token`.

get.summary: Get the per-member daily usage report
get.description: Settled managed usage of the caller's workspace in UTC day buckets, with one row per member per day: requests, input and output tokens, and the credits consumed. `from` and `to` snap to UTC day boundaries and may span up to 366 days; `to` defaults to now and never reaches past today. Each page holds up to `limit` buckets: while `hasMore` is true, repeat the request with `page` set to `nextPage`. A turn still in flight appears once it settles. Every page records a data access event in the audit trail.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the report, ISO 8601 date or date-time

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the report, exclusive, as an ISO 8601 date or date-time. One day is `from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-02`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Day buckets per page

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The `nextPage` of the previous response

400.description: `from` is missing or in the future, a date does not parse, the window is empty or longer than 366 days, or `page` is not a page of this report

get.description: The caller's most recent connector tool calls, newest first: which tool of which connector ran, whether it succeeded, failed or was blocked before it left, how long it took and when.

parameters.name: connectorId
parameters.description: Only calls to this connector.

get.description: The levels the caller has saved. A tool with no saved level takes its category's level when one is saved (reported with toolName `*read_only` or `*write`), and otherwise follows the account's approval policy.

put.description: Saves `allow`, `ask` or `deny` for one connector tool (`toolName`), for up to 200 of them at once (`toolNames`), or for a whole `category`. Send `toolName` or `toolNames` unless `category` is set. Whether a tool is destructive is decided by the server, and a `destructive` field in the body is ignored.

level.description: `allow` runs the tool without asking, `ask` asks every time, `deny` never runs it. A saved `allow` still asks when the call would send private data out after reading untrusted content.

category.description: Saves the level for a whole category of this connector's tools: its read-only tools, or its write and delete tools. A tool with no level of its own takes its category's level, including tools the connector adds later; an undeclared tool counts as write. May be sent with toolNames to set the listed tools in the same call.

destructive.description: Whether the server treats any of these tools as destructive

400.description: Missing connectorId, no tool or category, both toolName and toolNames, or an unknown level or category

403.description: A browser session sent no valid CSRF token

delete.description: Removes the saved level for one tool, or for every tool of the connector when `toolName` is omitted. Those tools then follow the account's approval policy again.

removed.description: How many saved levels were removed

400.description: Missing connectorId, or an empty toolName

403.description: A browser session sent no valid CSRF token
